newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: European Union "deplores" Israeli housing decision.
newsitem.headline: European Union "deplores" Israeli housing decision.

text.p: The European Union said on Wednesday it deeply deplored Israel's approval of the building of new Jewish housing in Arab East Jerusalem.

Earlier on Wednesday, Israel, ignoring warnings that the move could unleash a wave of Palestinian violence, approved the project to build the homes at Jabal Abu Ghneim, a tree-covered hill site between Jerusalem and Bethlehem which the Israelis call Har Homa and which they captured in the 1967 Middle East war.

"The EU deeply deplores the decision of the Israeli government to approve construction plans for Har Homa/Jabal Abu Ghneim located on the West Bank in the Jerusalem area," a statement issued by the Dutch EU presidency said.

"The EU has repeatedly stated that settlements in the occupied territories contravene international law and are a major obstacle to peace," the statement, issued by Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo in his role as chairman of the EU Council of Ministers, said.
It reaffirmed the EU's position that East Jerusalem was an occupied territory and was not under Israeli sovereignty.

"The EU calls on Israel to respect its obligations under international law, to refrain from measures that have an eroding effect on the confidence necessary for the further implementation of the (Middle East peace) agreements and prejudge the outcome of the permanent status negotiations," it said.
"The decision is especially regrettable since the signing of the Protocol on Hebron was a positive development which created a new momentum in the peace process..." it added.
